thread.title: Roku Beats First-Quarter Views, Sending Shares Higher - Investor's Business Daily

title: Roku Beats First-Quarter Views, Sending Shares Higher - Investor's Business Daily
text:
Streaming video platform Roku ( ROKU ) late Wednesday reported better-than-expected first-quarter results and guided higher for the current quarter and full year. But shares fluctuated between positive and negative ground in late trading.
X Roku lost an adjusted 7 cents a share in the March quarter as sales rose 36% year over year to $136.6 million. Analysts expected the company to lose 16 cents a share on sales of $128 million, according to Zacks Investment Research.
Active accounts rose 47% year over year to 20.8 million. Streaming hours increased 56% to 5.1 billion hours. Average revenue per user climbed 50% to $15.07.
Roku shares seesawed in after-hours trading on the stock market today . During the regular session, the stock jumped 8.9% to 36.08.
 For the current quarter, Roku expects to lose an adjusted $9.5 million on sales of $140 million, based on the midpoint of its guidance. It did not give a target for earnings per share. Wall Street was modeling it to lose 16 cents a share on sales of $136 million, Zacks said.
"Roku delivered another strong quarter of operational and financial performance in Q1 2018," Roku Chief Executive Anthony Wood and Chief Financial Officer Steve Louden said in a letter to shareholders . "The secular shift from legacy TV distribution to streaming continues unabated."
Roku Boasts Increased Scale Roku's advertising and content partners are benefiting from the company's increased scale, they said.
"Nearly half of our roughly 21 million active users have cut the cord or have never had a traditional pay-TV subscription, which means that they simply cannot be reached through linear TV," Wood and Louden said. "This makes our strategic position in the living room extremely valuable."
Roku licenses a smart-TV operating system to consumer electronics firms. It also makes its own set-top boxes and TV dongles for accessing internet television services.
Roku monetizes its platform and user base mostly through advertising sales. It also gets a share of sales from pay-per-view and subscription video-on-demand services.
The Los Gatos, Calif.-based company faces competition from rival streaming devices from Amazon ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ) and others, as well as TV makers opting for alternative operating systems.
Roku devices and smart TVs are a popular method for consumers to watch Netflix ( NFLX ), Hulu, Amazon Prime Video, YouTube and other internet video networks on their TVs.
